audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid tells the player "if you're behind on stacks just look to flash out or wait for it to end" during Realm of Death.
audit.why: Realm of Death moves both champions into a separate arena for its duration. Neither can leave until the timer expires or one dies — Flash only repositions you inside the realm, it does not remove you from it. Telling a losing Nasus to Flash out is advice that burns his Summoner and kills him anyway.
audit.corrected: You cannot leave Realm of Death, Flash included — plan to survive the duration, not to escape it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mordekaiser.json (R: 'drags his victim to a different dimension with him')

audit.whatIsWrong: Mordekaiser's passive Darkness Rise is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Darkness Rise is the engine of every extended trade he wins in this lane: after landing 3 attacks or spells on a champion he gains a persistent damage aura plus move speed. The whole early-game section explains that he wins long trades without ever naming the mechanic that does it, so the player has no idea the counterplay is to break off before the third hit.
audit.corrected: Name the 3-hit trigger and tell the player to disengage before the third attack or spell lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the Sands is described only as bonus HP and ult damage; its Siphoning Strike cooldown reduction and bonus attack range are never mentioned.
audit.why: Inside Realm of Death the fight is a pure 1v1 with a fixed duration, so the number of stacked Q casts Nasus lands is the entire outcome. Fury of the Sands reduces Siphoning Strike's cooldown and grants bonus attack range, which is precisely why popping it on the pull wins the realm — that is a mechanical reason, not a vibe.
audit.corrected: State that R grants bonus HP, bonus attack range, armour and MR, and a reduced Q cooldown, so you get more stacked Q casts inside the realm.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers claim Nasus out-sustains Indestructible ("your lifesteal eats through his W heal", "you out-sustain his W heal") with no mention of Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this: Mordekaiser sustains through chip damage via Indestructible (W), and Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades. Indestructible is a 12/11/10/9/8s zero-cost ability that stores damage he deals AND takes into a shield, which he then consumes as a heal. Grievous Wounds cuts the heal, not the shield, so it has to be applied before he cashes it — a timing point the content never makes.
audit.corrected: Tell the player to carry Grievous Wounds and land it before he consumes the shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: The resource asymmetry is never stated.
audit.why: Every Mordekaiser ability costs 0 (he uses Shield as a resource); Nasus pays 20 mana per Q, 80 per Wither and 60-100 per Spirit Fire. Morde can throw Q and E on cooldown forever while Nasus can and does run dry stacking, which is a real reason the early poke war is unwinnable.
audit.corrected: Note that his kit is free and yours is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns lists two abilities with no numbers at all.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140/120/100s — the longest and most punishable cooldown in the lane — and Indestructible is 12/11/10/9/8s. Neither number appears anywhere, so the player cannot actually time the windows the rest of the text tells them to trade around.
audit.corrected: Put the real numbers on the two cooldowns that decide the matchup.

edits.before: Mordekaiser owns these levels and you have to respect it — his Q does bonus damage when he hits you isolated, and his E can pull you off the wave into it, so don't stand alone next to him while you last-hit. Farm your Q stacks from max range, use Spirit Fire (E) to shove and stack safely, and never sit in his W shield-trade because his sustain beats yours before you have items. You have no Wither until 3, and even then a single point won't save an extended fight — give ground and concede the lane.
edits.after: Mordekaiser owns these levels and you have to respect it — his Q does bonus damage when he hits you isolated, and his E can pull you off the wave into it, so don't stand alone next to him while you last-hit. Watch his passive: three attacks or spells landed turns on Darkness Rise, the damage aura and move speed that wins his long trades — break off before the third. Farm Q stacks at max range and Spirit Fire the wave. Every Morde ability costs zero, so he never runs dry and you do. Give ground.

edits.before: At 6 his Realm of Death (R) is the whole game — it yanks you into a 1v1 and steals your stats, and it hits hardest while you're unstacked and squishy. The counter is timing: the moment he ults you, pop Fury of the Sands so you fight inside your own bonus HP and ult damage, and slap Wither on him to kill his attack speed and chase. If you can survive his R window you bleed him out, but if you're behind on stacks just look to flash out or wait for it to end — don't trade your stat block into his.
edits.after: At 6 his Realm of Death (R) is the whole game — it yanks you into a 1v1, steals your stats, and you cannot leave it. Flash does not get you out, so never plan around escaping. The moment he ults, pop Fury of the Sands: bonus HP, bonus attack range and a shorter Q cooldown mean you land more stacked Qs inside the realm than you ever would outside it. Wither him on contact — he has no dash, so the realm traps him too. Grievous Wounds before he cashes Indestructible decides the long fight.

edits.before: His R drags you into a 1v1 and steals your stats, so it swings hardest when you are unstacked — pop Fury of the Sands the instant you are pulled in to fight on your terms.
edits.after: His R drags you into a 1v1 and steals your stats — and you cannot leave it, Flash included. Pop Fury of the Sands the instant you land: bonus HP, attack range and a faster Q.

edits.before: Stacked Q plus Wither's attack-speed and move-speed shred turn his no-dash, single-target kit into a free duel — you out-sustain his W heal.
edits.after: Stacked Q plus Wither's attack-speed and move-speed shred turn his no-dash kit into a free duel — but bring Grievous Wounds or Indestructible undoes it.

edits.before: Ult you while you are unstacked so Realm of Death steals a fat, low-DPS stat block
edits.after: Ult you the moment Fury of the Sands is down so the realm is a free stat check

edits.before: - Mordekaiser Realm of Death: matchup-defining — His 1v1 realm. Wither him inside it. Track it before every engage. - Mordekaiser Death’s Grasp: Pulls enemies toward him after a delay + passive magic pen. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Mordekaiser Realm of Death: matchup-defining — a 140/120/100s 1v1 realm you cannot leave. Wither him inside it. - Mordekaiser Indestructible: 12/11/10/9/8s shield he cashes as a heal — land Grievous Wounds before he does.

notes: DATA-QUALITY WARNING for the kit builder, not this matchup: the derived `grounding` flag fires on the word "ground" used as terrain. champ-data/_kits/mordekaiser.json flags Q ("smashes the ground") as grounding, and the same false positive appears on Olaf Q ("throws an axe into the ground"), Ornn Q ("slams the ground") and Poppy Q. Poppy W is the only genuine grounding in my slice — its text actually says "slowed and grounded". I wrote no advice off any of the suspect flags. Separately: Mordekaiser's E magic-penetration passive asserted in breakdown.cooldowns is not in the Data Dragon text, so I left that string's claim untouched rather than confirm or remove it.
